title: Chess, But My Pawns Can Reproduce
summary: Chess vs Stockfish where the player's (White's) pawns follow Conway's Game of Life. After each White move, one generation is computed for White pawns: a pawn with 0-1 white-pawn neighbours dies (solitude), 4+ neighbours dies (overpopulation), 2-3 survives, and an empty square with exactly 3 white-pawn neighbours spawns a new white pawn. Game 1 is lost after the pawns die out; game 2 is won (bishop + two knights mate); a third 'pawns-only' attempt fails.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600). Only White's pawns follow Game of Life; Black's pawns are normal.
After every White move a Game of Life generation runs on White pawns, using the 8 neighbouring squares and counting only white pawns as neighbours [inferred: 'my pawns follow the rules'].
Survival: a white pawn with 2 or 3 white-pawn neighbours survives; 0-1 or 4+ dies (is removed).
Birth: an EMPTY square with exactly 3 white-pawn neighbours gains a new white pawn (all births/deaths simultaneous).
The pawn just moved is evaluated too (e.g. 1.e4 pawn died having no neighbours); births can appear deep in enemy territory and promote normally when reaching rank 8.
Squares occupied by other pieces cannot spawn pawns [inferred].
